description: Issue #839: a cross-depth duplicate in the NESTED-FIRST orientation. `dup` is declared inside `define outer` on line 2 and again at the top level on line 6, and `params.original_span` names the NESTED one — because "earlier" is a property of source order, not of depth. `spec/execution-model.md:86-87` is explicit that it is "a name an EARLIER declaration in the program already registered" that raises. Its mirror is `nested-duplicate-definition` (top-level first). Both orientations are needed: a two-pass registration that visited every top-level declaration before descending — a plausible "so forward references resolve" refactor — preserves the top-level-first orientation and INVERTS this one, flagging the line-2 declaration as the duplicate and naming line 6 as the original, so the learner stands on the earlier line and is told they already defined it later. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
